text:
devon: Heads up — seeing apiserver 503 spikes in eu-west1 starting ~08:12 UTC, coincident with a batch of GPU node onboards from the new spot pool.
sofia: timeline? graphs? any leader flips in etcd?
devon: attaching snippets from the controlplane logs (trimmed):
```
2026-03-21T08:12:18Z apiserver error: proxy: upstream response 503
2026-03-21T08:12:19Z watch queue backlog: duration=5.2s pending=1290
2026-03-21T08:12:20Z controller-manager: workqueue requeues spiking
2026-03-21T08:12:22Z etcd: leader changed from 10.0.10.5 to 10.0.12.7 (election took 1.1s)
```
lee: I checked the new GPU nodes — sashimi-spot-*-eu has MTU set to 1400 while the controlplane expects 1500. Getting lots of TCP retransmits and kube-proxy conntrack churn.
mike: MTU mismatch = classic watch disconnects. Can we cordon the new pool and drain? That should stop new connections while we investigate.
sofia: Can we confirm conntrack/NAT exhaustion? ops-bot, any alerts fired?
ops-bot: Alert: apiserver_503_rate high (eu-west1) at 08:13 UTC. Related: high_conntrack_count on nodes sashimi-spot-01..04.
lee: output from one of the nodes:
```
$ ip link show dev eth0
2: eth0: mtu 1400 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
$ ss -s | grep retrans
TCP: retrans: 823 total
$ sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count = 65530
```
anita: 65k conntrack ~= near default conntrack max (65536). When conntrack fills, kube-proxy NAT stops accepting new ephemeral ports -> apiserver proxies start 503-ing.
mike: immediate mitigation: cordon + drain the spot pool, bump conntrack max on controlplane-facing nodes, and scale up apiserver replicas by 1 for a short window.
devon: I'm cordoning sashimi-spot-01..04 now. Running drain with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data.
sofia: Do we want to increase nf_conntrack max clusterwide? That has memory cost; prefer to fix MTU and onboarding script so nodes come up with 1500.
lee: onboarding script bug: cloud-init sets mtu from image default (1400) because of a new CNI config in the custom GPU AMI. Will patch the AMI and re-create the pool.
mike: For short term can we set: sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144 on the node pool (and controlplane proxies)? That's a cheap stopgap.
anita: Agree but document cost: conntrack table growth increases kernel memory; on small controlplane instances could OOM if we go too high. We should only do this transiently.
devon: Executed: cordoned + drained 04 nodes, bumped conntrack to 200k on affected nodes and apiserver replicas scaled 3->4. 503s dropped after ~45s :thumbsup:
sofia: Nice. Follow-ups: (1) patch GPU AMI to correct MTU; (2) add a preprovision check in the autoscaler to verify MTU matches controlplane; (3) add a test in CI that boots one GPU instance and validates conntrack and MTU; (4) consider reserved capacity for core pools to avoid spot thrash.
mike: Also: consider increasing apiserver keepalive and client-side retry/backoff for controller-manager to tolerate short network hiccups. Might reduce tail SLO impact.
lee: I'll own AMI fix and autoscaler pre-checks. Planning to flip tomorrow morning EU maintenance window.
anita: I'll write the short runbook for conntrack bump + cordon steps and the memory caveats.
ops-bot: Incident resolved at 08:14:25 UTC. Postmortem tag: controlplane-networking-gpu-onboard-mtu.

devon: Thanks everyone — closing this thread. We'll follow up with the runbook and AMI patch PRs. :eyes:
